Refusal assertions must inspect unchanged state.; the language is measured rather than assumed: conformance/src/rules-probe installs the same bounded Rules programs into the pinned official Firestore emulator and into fireemu and compares every verdict (680 claims in conformance/rules-matrix.json, 22 whole-program probes in conformance/rules-programs.json); query proofs are sound, not complete: a rule that reads an unconstrained field denies the query; the principal request.auth is built from follows the compatibility profile on both the Firestore and the Storage Rules surfaces (see AUTH-RULES-1); the rules themselves are evaluated identically under both profiles; request.query.orderBy is a map from field path to "ASC" / "DESC", request.query.limit is null without a limit, and request.resource and request.query are absent rather than null on a request that has neither; string.matches() / replace(): the RE2 surface the official runtime has -- capturing groups with $0 / $1 expansion, the inline flags (?i) (?s) (?m), POSIX and Unicode classes, hex escapes -- and, as in RE2, no lookarounds and no backreferences; a literal pattern is compiled while the ruleset is, so an unusable one fails the load; capture-free alternatives whose branches each consume one character repeat iteratively at constant match depth; every attempted branch remains charged to the regex step budget, and patterns with captures or multi-character branches keep the general matcher; a recursive call and a call chain of more than twenty calls are compile errors, with the official compiler's messages; three language rows are documented divergences, all the same one: the official compiler's static type checker rejects at load what fireemu raises at evaluation; the request decision is the same; conformance: firestore/rules-decisions (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production; each number is measured against the pinned official emulator, not read off the documentation: ten document accesses are served and eleven are denied, thirty accesses of one path are served, and the call-depth boundary is the one its compiler reports (conformance/rules-programs.json); request.auth from verified ID tokens on every Firestore surface; Bearer owner bypasses; the compatibility profile decides how much verification a caller's token must survive: under firebase the unsigned mock tokens the official emulators admit are admitted too (an unknown sub, an exp nobody reads), so @firebase/rules-unit-testing works unchanged; under strict the issuer, audience, virtual-clock expiry, subject and revocation are all checked; two checks stay on in both profiles, and spec/compatibility/contract.json records them as deliberate divergences of the emulator profile: the audience must name the routed Firestore resource project or Storage bucket project, and a token that claims to be signed must verify against the session key; a valid bare Storage bucket routed through the default session binds emulator-profile mock tokens to that bucket's project namespace without changing object ownership, tenancy, App Check, fault injection or resumable-upload routing, and without registering a session; under the emulator profile, queries whose composite index is not configured are served with an FS&#95;EMULATOR&#95;INDEX&#95;ASSUMED warning, like the Firebase Emulator Suite; under strict (the default) they are refused with FAILED&#95;PRECONDITION and the firestore.indexes.json fragment, and the index merges production performs (equality filters served by several composite indexes that share the order suffix, verified against a real project on 2026-09-08) are accepted; the index policy has no configuration key of its own: it follows the profile; firestore.enforceLimits follows the profile with an explicit override: under strict a Standard query limit violation refuses the query with INVALID&#95;ARGUMENT, under emulator it is reported as an FS&#95;LIMIT&#95;OBSERVED:&lt;limit id&gt; warning and the query runs; conformance: firestore/missing-composite-index (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production; the query limits the pinned official emulator refuses as well -- more than 30 DNF disjunctions ('IN' over 30 values) and a second array-contains clause (FAILED&#95;PRECONDITION) -- stay refused under the emulator profile (fireemu&#95;adapter&#95;grpc::gateway::OFFICIAL&#95;EMULATOR&#95;REFUSES) |
| FS-TRANSACTIONS: Transactions and contention / Standard / Native; configured concurrency mode must be read back; transaction tokens and retry paths | Implemented, unverified | 1 / 0 | Not attested | Not attested | Not attested | Edition does not determine the observed database concurrency mode. Exact timeout, retry and ordering assertions remain to be mapped.; pessimistic locking, as production runs it (concurrencyMode PESSIMISTIC): every document a read-write transaction read and every range it queried or listed is locked until the transaction finishes; a commit outside the transaction that touches a locked document waits for the release (15 s in the daemon) and is then refused with ABORTED 'Too much contention on these documents. Please try again.' in production's words, and the transaction's own commit succeeds; two transactions that both read a document and both commit into it are the deadlock production resolves by aborting one side: the first committer is aborted with the same retryable ABORTED for its client to retry, the second commits; the official Local Emulator Suite locks the same way and refuses the out-of-band writer with ABORTED 'Transaction lock timeout.', so the transaction-concurrency rows of the semantics matrix are parity on status and code (conformance/firestore-production-matrix.json, transactions/lifecycle, recorded against production 2026-09-05); conformance: firestore/transaction-read-set-abort (conformance/README.md) |
